newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa shows minor losses as origins sell.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa shows minor losses as origins sell.

text.p: London cocoa futures pencilled in minor losses on Thursday as sterling's relentless surge put a dampener on the market's latest rally by triggering West African sales.

Activity was thin however, and benchmark March cocoa drew some support in early afternoon from New York's challenge of the key $1,400 but slipped back again as the UK currency struck fresh highs against the dollar and mark.
Sterling reached a new four-year high of $1.6905 in early afternoon, then eased slightly to trade around $1.6875 by 1730 GMT.
Cocoa traders also cited price fixing by West African shippers who were long of December futures.
March cocoa ended three stg down at 925 stg a tonne after trading in a narrow range between 923 and 929 throughout the session. December lost four stg to 889.
On Wednesday, it broke free of a tight downtrend channel which had formed solid barriers over the market for over a month.
Volume totalled an unimpressive 2,861 lots, which included a large number of AAs. E.D. & F Man was an active seller, traders said. On the switches, Dec/March saw deals at 35-36 stg.
Traders dismissed comments by the Ivorian Prime Minister Daniel Kablan Duncan in Brussels suggesting that the total cocoa crop would be around 950,000 tonnes in the 1996/97 season.
"It's meaningless. They are never right," said one.
Estimates of arrivals in the first half of November, now pegged at between 130,000 and 175,000 tonnes, were too wide to make any assessments, traders said.
One sticking issue in Ivorian shipments is freight rates which have yet to be announced by the government.
Technical support on March cocoa is pegged at 917-914 stg. --Clelia Oziel, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8072
